glosses: to specialize (someone for something)
to specialize (become specialized)
ukierunkowywać na wybrany obszar

examples.text: Często odnosił wrażenie, że Leonard, który pchnął intelekt na nieodkryte dotąd wyżyny, znalazł tam duże i specjalizowane złoża głupoty.

glosses: To make distinct or separate from what is common
To go into specific details.

examples.text: Firſt laſh the Great-ones ; but, if thou be wiſe, / In generall, and doe not ſpeciallize : / Yet, if thou doe, ſo wiſely let it be, / None may except but thoſe that faulty be.

glosses: To make distinct or separate from what is common
To specify: to mention specifically.

examples.text: Our Sauiour specialising and nominating the places in which these false prophets should teach his presence to be.

glosses: To make distinct or separate from what is common
To narrow in scope.

examples.text: He is at moſt a confuſed and wild Chriſtian, not ſpecialized by any form, but capable of all.

glosses: To make distinct or separate from what is common
To make distinct or separate due to form or function.

examples.text: In the lowest orders of being, we find these functions very much blended together, and several of them apparently performed by one simple apparatus ; but in proportion as we rise in the scale, we perceive that they are specialized, or separated from each other, and that a complicated set of organs is appropriated to each of them.

Those who insist that a woman’s place is at home by divine decree need only to study the life of primitive man to find out how very human are some of our domestic customs, for they will then see this distinction, that while nature has specialized woman for child-bearing, it is society which has specialized her for housework.

glosses: To become distinct or separate from what is common, particularly

examples.text: These cells specialized for propagation, however they may originate, are accordingly distinguished by a special name, that of Spores of Sporules.

glosses: To become distinct or separate from what is common
To focus one's study upon a particular skill, field, topic, or genre.

examples.text: Also, to their honour be it said, they will not allow their scholars to specialize, and, with four hours of mathematics a week, even a Newton would not go up to Cambridge knowing much.

glosses: To become distinct or separate from what is common
To focus one's business upon a particular item or service.

examples.text: Firms... which have specialised in the manufacture of ‘heavies’...

Blackhead: I might look you up myself one of these days. Do you specialise at all, like?
Penny Guy: Yeah. Verbal abuse and colonic irrigation.

glosses: To become distinct or separate from what is common
To be known or notorious for some specialty.

examples.text: Watson specializes in adiposeness; none of his chorus beauties may be considered featherweights.

glosses: To train (someone) in a specialty.

examples.text: "Kia, Honey, you got to help him to it," Bell Norton told the 16 year old girl she was "specializing" as part of the hospital's intensive care program for high risk babies and mothers.

glosses: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of specialize.

examples.text: Our Sauiour specialising and nominating the places in which these false prophets should teach his presence to be.
Firms... which have specialised in the manufacture of ‘heavies’...
Some centres specialise in timber, and those conveniently situated to the coalfields deal with large quantities of pit props.
Jim is a nurseryman, specialising in clematis, and he has built up a business exporting 150 varieties to countries all over the world.
[Oily Cart] specialises in creating spectacular productions for young people with complex disabilities.
